title: Attend to Mixed Feed Processing Operations

lessons.title: Starting up and running a pellet line
lessons.html:
Starting up and running a pellet line

At this level you take responsibility for operating the processing line to specification, optimising throughput and quality, and guiding junior operators.

Pre-start checks

  1. Confirm the product, die specification (hole size and thickness) and conditioning targets from the production order and process specification.
  2. Inspect the die and rollers: wear, blocked holes, roller gap set as the SOP specifies.
  3. Check knives, door seals and the overload protection (shear pin or torque limiter).
  4. Drain condensate from steam lines; check steam pressure and that the steam trap station works.
  5. Check cooler, crumbler roll gap (if crumbling), screener decks and aspiration.
  6. Check the pellet bin has enough mash of the correct product.

Start-up sequence

  1. Start downstream equipment first: finished bin conveying, screener, cooler, cooler fan, then the pellet mill main motor and conditioner.
  2. Start the feeder at low rate with dry mash to warm and prime the die.
  3. Introduce steam gradually and bring conditioner temperature to target.
  4. Increase feed rate step by step while watching motor amps, conditioner temperature and pellet appearance.
  5. Divert the first off-spec pellets to rework if the procedure requires.

Optimising the run

ObservationLikely causeResponse
Amps rising, risk of chokeFeed rate too high, wet steamReduce feed rate, check traps
Soft pellets, high finesLow conditioning temperature, worn dieAdjust within spec, report die wear
Dark, burnt pelletsExcessive temperature or frictionLower temperature, check die
Hot pellets after coolerCooler overloaded or bed too shallowAdjust discharge and airflow

Record process readings at the set interval: throughput, amps, steam pressure, conditioner temperature, cooler outlet temperature, and durability test results.

lessons.title: Quality checks, shutdown and troubleshooting
lessons.html:
Quality checks, shutdown and troubleshooting

In-process quality checks

  • Pellet durability index (PDI) on samples at the set frequency.
  • Pellet length and diameter visually against the standard.
  • Product temperature and moisture after the cooler.
  • Fines percentage after screening.
  • For crumbles, particle size against the specification.
  • For heat-treated feeds with hygiene targets, confirm conditioning temperature and time records meet the critical limit; product below the limit is held and reported.

Record results and act on out-of-spec readings using the adjustments you are authorised to make. Escalate anything beyond your authority.

Changeovers

  • Run the pellet bin down; follow the flush and sequencing plan.
  • Change the die when the next product needs a different specification; use the die lifting device, never manual lifting.
  • Clear the conditioner of the previous product as the SOP requires.

Controlled shutdown

  1. Reduce feed rate and switch to dry mash or oily flush to leave the die holes filled for a clean restart, as the SOP says.
  2. Close steam, stop the feeder and conditioner, then the main motor.
  3. Let the cooler and screener run empty before stopping.

Clearing a die choke safely

  1. Stop the feeder and steam.
  2. Isolate and lock out the main motor and feeder; verify zero energy.
  3. Wear heat-resistant gloves; the die and chamber are hot.
  4. Clear the chamber as the SOP specifies; drill or press out blocked holes where required.
  5. Find and record the cause before restarting.

Guiding others

Show junior operators how to read amps and conditioner trends, explain why each step matters, and check their records. Insist on lockout every time.

Key points

  • Check die, rollers, steam quality and cooler before start-up.
  • Start downstream first and bring steam and feed rate up gradually.
  • Use amps, temperatures and pellet quality to optimise the run.
  • Hold product that fails a hygiene critical limit.
  • Lock out and verify before clearing chokes.

quiz.question: Motor amps are rising and a choke is likely. What is the first response?

options.text: Reduce feed rate and check steam traps

quiz.question: Pellets are soft with high fines. A likely cause is:

options.text: Low conditioning temperature or worn die

quiz.question: Heat-treated feed fails the conditioning critical limit. What should happen?

options.text: Send it to the customer anyway
Hold the product and report it

quiz.question: How should a heavy die be changed?
Why let the cooler and screener run empty at shutdown?

options.text: So product does not remain inside
